cleanIntro:
This guide follows Fabarm's over & under manual, the book Syren publishes for the Elos N2 Elevate. The book prints no model name and never prints "Syren" or "Elevate", so check your variant against it. Every step here is the book's general over & under procedure, stated as generally as the book states it.

The gun comes apart in three pieces: forend, barrels, then the stock and action frame left together. Fabarm stops there. ⚠ The forend never turns more than about 12° off the barrels.

steps.title: Safety on: S showing on the tang
steps.action: This guide follows Fabarm's over & under manual, the book Syren publishes for the Elos N2 Elevate. It prints no model name, so check your variant against it. Point the muzzles in a safe direction and slide the safety catch on the top tang back toward the stock until the S shows.
steps.prose: Moving the catch left or right only picks which barrel fires first. It does not put the gun on safe; only sliding it back does.
steps.quote: The shotgun is ON SAFE when the catch has been moved to the rear (towards the stock, when the letter “S” appears on the action frame tang)
steps.cite: Fabarm over & under Use and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — SAFETY AND BARREL SELECTOR, printed p.13
steps.warn: Never take someone’s word that the gun is unloaded, but always check it yourself with your fingers off the trigger and the gun pointed in a safe direction.

steps.title: Top lever across, both chambers emptied and checked
steps.action: Push the top lever across and open the gun. Take any shells out of both chambers, then look into each chamber yourself before you go on.
steps.prose: If your gun has automatic ejectors, a fired shell is thrown clear when the gun opens and an unfired one is only lifted. Open it where you can see where a case lands.
steps.aside: For shotguns with automatic ejectors, the spent shotshell will be ejected from the gun when it is opened, whilst an unfired shotshell will simply be extracted to facilitate its removal.
steps.quote: Prior to cleaning the gun, make sure that it is not loaded!
steps.cite: Fabarm over & under Use and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — CLEANING, printed p.15

steps.title: Stock under your right arm, gun closed
steps.action: Close the empty gun and hold the stock firmly under your right arm. The forend comes off first, the same way it comes off the barrels when the gun is new from the box.
steps.prose: Fabarm's disassembly sends you back to the first two points of its assembly section for the forend. The next step is those two points.
steps.quote: Holding the stock firmly under your right arm, take out the forend following the points 1. and 2. of the paragraph ASSEMBLY.
steps.cite: Fabarm over & under Use and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY, Step 1, printed p.15

steps.title: Forend catch open, forend turned no more than 12°, out diagonally
steps.action: Unlock the forend catch and carefully rotate the forend away from the barrels, no further than about 12°. Then slide the forend off the barrels diagonally.
steps.prose: Twelve degrees is a small angle. If the forend will not come away at that angle, do not lever it further.
steps.aside: Remove the forend from the barrel, sliding it in a diagonal direction
steps.quote: unlock the forend catch (FIG. 4) and carefully rotate the forend from the barrel. Do not exceed a rotation of 12° as indicated on the Fig.5
steps.cite: Fabarm over & under Use and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — ASSEMBLY, first and second points, printed p.14

steps.title: Open the gun and lift the barrels off
steps.action: Open the gun with the top lever and carefully lift the barrels off the action frame.
steps.prose: Go gently: the barrel hook and the hinge pins are bearing surfaces, and forcing them marks the surfaces that keep the gun in line.
steps.quote: Open the shotgun and carefully disengage the barrel from the action frame.
steps.cite: Fabarm over & under Use and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY, Step 2, printed p.15

steps.title: Forend back on the barrels for safe keeping
steps.action: With the barrels off, put the forend back on them carefully, so it is not damaged while the gun is apart.
steps.prose: A loose forend on the bench is the part that gets knocked off and scratched.
steps.quote: Carefully reinstall the forend on the barrel. This will avoid damaging the forend.
steps.cite: Fabarm over & under Use and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY, Step 2, printed p.15

steps.title: Top lever: released from the bottom of the action frame if needed
steps.action: If the top lever needs releasing with the barrels off, push the cocking lever in the bottom of the action frame.
steps.prose: Only do this if you need to. Fabarm gives it as an option, not a required step.
steps.quote: The top lever can if necessary be release by pushing the cocking lever located in the bottom of the action frame.
steps.cite: Fabarm over & under Use and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY, Step 3, printed p.15

steps.title: ⛔ Field strip complete: Fabarm stops here
steps.action: Forend, barrels, and the stock with the action frame. That is the whole strip Fabarm gives the owner. Do not take the action, trigger or stock apart any further. Changing choke tubes, if your barrels take them, is under DEEP CLEAN.
steps.prose: Anything past this point is work for your gun dealer or a gunsmith.
steps.quote: DO NOT STRIP YOUR SHOTGUN ANY FURTHER.
steps.cite: Fabarm over & under Use and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.15

steps.title: Bores: cleaned and oiled after every session
steps.action: Clean the inside of both barrels and leave a coat of oil in them after every shooting session.
steps.prose: Fabarm also says the bore must be perfectly dry before the first shot of the day, so run a flannel through the barrels before you shoot.
steps.quote: The inside of the barrel must be cleaned and oiled after every session of shooting.
steps.cite: Fabarm over & under Use and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — CLEANING: BARREL, printed p.15

steps.title: Bearing surfaces: perfectly clean, a light film of oil
steps.action: Clean the bearing surfaces, the places that rub and take pressure when the gun opens and closes, and leave them with a light film of oil.
steps.prose: These are the barrel hook, the hinge pins, the lumps and the forend iron. Grit left on them wears the fit of the gun.
steps.quote: The bearing surfaces are subject to friction and pressure when opening and closing the gun and must always be perfectly clean and coated with a light film of oil.
steps.cite: Fabarm over & under Use and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — CLEANING: BEARING SURFACE, printed p.15
steps.warn: Do not apply too much oil on the action frame so as to avoid making the wood spongy.

steps.title: Outside metal wiped with an oiled cloth; wood with linseed oil
steps.action: Wipe the outside metal with a lightly oiled cloth and take off every fingerprint. From time to time, give the wood a moderate coat of linseed oil with a cloth that does not shed lint.
steps.prose: Fingerprints are where rust starts on blued metal.
steps.aside: It is also recommended to oil the shotgun lightly each time it is submitted to bad handling or severe atmospheric conditions.
steps.quote: Clean the external metallic surfaces of the gun with a lightly oiled cloth and wipe off any trace of fingerprints.
steps.cite: Fabarm over & under Use and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — CLEANING: EXTERNAL METALLIC SURFACES, printed p.15

deepSteps.title: Choke tubes: unloaded, on safe, action open
deepSteps.action: If your barrels take choke tubes: unload the gun, put the safety on and open the action before a choke tube is touched.
deepSteps.prose: Not every Fabarm over & under is delivered with choke tubes. If yours has fixed chokes, this lane does not apply.
deepSteps.quote: Place the safety in the “on safe” position and open the action.
deepSteps.cite: Fabarm over & under Use and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — REMOVING/INSTALLING CHOKE TUBES, Step 1, printed p.16
deepSteps.warn: Unload the firearm before changing choke tubes.

deepSteps.title: Choke wrench in, turned counter-clockwise
deepSteps.action: Fit the choke tube wrench into the choke tube and turn it counter-clockwise to remove the tube.
deepSteps.prose: Counter-clockwise as you face the muzzle takes the tube out.
deepSteps.quote: Turn the wrench counter-clockwise to remove the choke tube.
deepSteps.cite: Fabarm over & under Use and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — REMOVING/INSTALLING CHOKE TUBES, Step 3, printed p.16

deepSteps.title: Back in clockwise: tight, never over-tightened
deepSteps.action: Put a small amount of lubricant on the threads, insert the tube, and screw it in clockwise until tight. Check it is tight with the choke wrench, but do not over-tighten it.
deepSteps.prose: A little lubricant on the threads is what lets the tube come out easily next time.
deepSteps.aside: A small amount of lubricate on the treads will ensure the choke tube can be installed and removed with ease.
deepSteps.quote: Screw it in clockwise until tight. Make certain it is tight using the choke wrench but do not over tighten.
deepSteps.cite: Fabarm over & under Use and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — REMOVING/INSTALLING CHOKE TUBES, Step 5, printed p.16

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Check the tubes periodically, and never fire without one
deepSteps.action: Check periodically that each choke tube has not loosened. A barrel made for choke tubes is never fired without a tube installed.
deepSteps.prose: That is the last thing the book gives the owner to do to the barrels.
deepSteps.quote: Check the choke tube periodically to make sure the tube has not loosened.
deepSteps.cite: Fabarm over & under Use and Maintenance Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — REMOVING/INSTALLING CHOKE TUBES, Step 6, printed p.16
deepSteps.warn: DO NOT FIRE THIS SHOTGUN WITHOUT HAVING A CHOKE TUBE INSTALLED.

cleaning.name: BARRELS
tasks: Inside of both barrels cleaned and oiled after every session
Bore run dry with a flannel before the first shot of the day

cleaning.name: BEARING SURFACES
tasks: Surfaces that rub on opening and closing: perfectly clean, light film of oil
Do not over-oil the action frame; excess oil soaks into the wood

cleaning.name: OUTSIDE METAL AND WOOD
tasks: Outside metal wiped with a lightly oiled cloth, fingerprints off
Oiled lightly again after rough handling, rain, high humidity or salt air
Wood: a moderate coat of linseed oil from time to time, with a lint-free cloth

reassembly: Chambers checked empty before the gun goes back together.
One or two drops of oil on the front and sides of the barrel hook, the sides of the lumps and the forend iron. No more than that.
Forend off the barrels again: catch unlocked, turned no more than about 12°, slid off diagonally.
Stock held under your right arm, top lever opened with your right thumb, barrel hook fitted onto the action frame hinge pins with your left hand.
Hook held hard against the hinge pins, barrels rotated closed, top lever released. Let the top lever return on its own; it does not need to line up with the barrels.
Forend iron placed against the action frame at the same angle of about 12°, then rotated up against the barrels until the forend catch locks with an audible click.
⚠ Never force anything. If the barrels are not seated or not in line, forcing only damages the bearing surfaces.
fncheck: With both chambers confirmed empty and the muzzles in a safe direction, close the gun and check the top lever has returned on its own and the barrels are locked. Check the forend is locked to the barrels. Slide the safety back and confirm the S shows on the tang. If anything did not go back the way it came out, take the shotgun to your gun dealer or a gunsmith before firing it.
